title: Africa General Knowledge
description: 36 original questions celebrating Africa's geography, wildlife, ancient kingdoms, landmarks, and heritage (Multiple Choice & Free-Text).
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: What is the largest hot desert in the world, stretching across North Africa?
questions.explanation: The Sahara spans roughly 9.2 million square kilometers across eleven nations.

questions.prompt: Which mountain in Tanzania is the highest peak in Africa?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano rising 5,895 meters above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which African country is home to the Great Pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid of Khufu is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

questions.prompt: What is the largest lake in Africa by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is bordered by Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

questions.prompt: Which large island nation lies off the southeastern coast of mainland Africa?
questions.explanation: Madagascar is famous for its unique endemic lemurs and baobab trees.

questions.prompt: Which is Africa's most populous country?
questions.explanation: Nigeria has over 240 million residents in West Africa.

questions.prompt: Which famous waterfall sits on the Zambezi River between Zambia and Zimbabwe?
questions.explanation: Locally called Mosi-oa-Tunya ('The Smoke That Thunders'), Victoria Falls is over 1.7 km wide.

questions.prompt: Which East African national park in Tanzania is famous for the annual Great Wildebeest Migration?
questions.explanation: Over a million wildebeest and zebras migrate across the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem.

questions.prompt: Which African country has three official capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein?
questions.explanation: South Africa separates its executive, legislative, and judicial capitals.

questions.prompt: Which major river flows northward through Sudan and Egypt into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: The Nile is historically the lifeblood of northeastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which North African country is the largest in Africa by total land area?
questions.explanation: Algeria became Africa's largest country by area in 2011.

questions.prompt: Which fastest land animal on Earth inhabits African savannas?
questions.explanation: Cheetahs can accelerate to speeds around 100–110 km/h in short bursts.

questions.prompt: Which West African city in Mali was a renowned medieval center of Islamic scholarship and manuscripts?
questions.explanation: Timbuktu's Sankore libraries preserved hundreds of thousands of historic manuscripts.

questions.prompt: Which African country is the only one that was never formally colonized by a European power (aside from a brief WWII occupation)?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia defeated Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa in 1896.

questions.prompt: Which deep African river is the world's deepest river and crosses the equator twice?
questions.explanation: Parts of the Congo River plunge over 220 meters deep.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range runs across Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia?
questions.explanation: The Atlas Mountains separate the Mediterranean coast from the Sahara.

questions.prompt: Which East African valley is a massive geological trench containing several Great Lakes?
questions.explanation: The East African Rift is slowly splitting the Somali plate from the Nubian plate.

questions.prompt: Which African country is the world's largest producer of cocoa beans?
questions.explanation: Ivory Coast produces roughly 40% of the world's cocoa supply.

questions.prompt: Which famous coastal desert in southwestern Africa meets the cold Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Namib is considered one of the oldest deserts on Earth.

questions.prompt: Which landmark Cape near Cape Town is famous in maritime history?
questions.explanation: Portuguese navigator Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape in 1488.

questions.prompt: Which ancient stone city ruins in southern Africa gave modern Zimbabwe its name?
questions.explanation: Built between the 11th and 15th centuries, Great Zimbabwe was a thriving trade capital.

questions.prompt: In which country is the Serengeti's neighboring Ngorongoro Crater located?
questions.explanation: Ngorongoro is the world's largest inactive, intact volcanic caldera.

questions.prompt: Which landlocked African nation is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.explanation: Lesotho is the only independent state that lies entirely above 1,000 meters elevation.

questions.prompt: Which African city hosts the headquarters of the African Union?
questions.explanation: Addis Ababa in Ethiopia has hosted the OAU/AU since 1963.

questions.prompt: Which African lake is the second-deepest freshwater lake in the world after Lake Baikal?
questions.explanation: Lake Tanganyika reaches a maximum depth of 1,470 meters.

questions.prompt: Which inland river delta in Botswana never reaches the ocean, instead fanning out into the Kalahari?
questions.explanation: The Okavango Delta is a UNESCO World Heritage wildlife oasis.

questions.prompt: Which 14th-century ruler of the Mali Empire is famed for his legendary wealth and pilgrimage to Mecca?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's 1324 caravan put Mali prominently on medieval world maps.

questions.prompt: Which medieval Ethiopian town is famous for eleven monolithic churches carved straight down into solid volcanic rock?
questions.explanation: Lalibela's rock-hewn churches date from the 12th and 13th centuries.

questions.prompt: Which small African country is the smallest on the African mainland by land area?
questions.explanation: The Gambia follows the winding Gambia River and is surrounded by Senegal.

questions.prompt: Which African island archipelago in the Indian Ocean is the smallest sovereign African nation overall?
questions.explanation: Seychelles spans 115 granite and coral islands covering 459 km² of land.

questions.prompt: Which ancient kingdom centered in northern Ethiopia erected giant carved granite obelisks (stelae)?
questions.explanation: Aksum was a major Red Sea trading power from the 1st to 8th centuries CE.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Africa from the Arabian Peninsula at the southern end of the Red Sea?
questions.explanation: Bab-el-Mandeb lies between Djibouti/Eritrea and Yemen.

questions.prompt: Which African country has the highest number of ancient pyramids in the world (over 200)?
questions.explanation: The Kingdom of Kush built steep-sided pyramids at Meroë, Nuri, and El-Kurru.

questions.prompt: Which West African river flows in a giant boomerang arc through Guinea, Mali, Niger, and Nigeria?
questions.explanation: At 4,180 km, the Niger is Africa's third-longest river.

questions.prompt: Which extreme geothermal depression in northeastern Ethiopia is one of the hottest inhabited places on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Danakil Depression features colorful sulfur springs and salt flats below sea level.

questions.prompt: Which island off Tanzania's coast was historically a famed hub of the East African spice trade?
questions.explanation: Zanzibar's Stone Town blends Swahili, Arab, Persian, and Indian architecture.
